rule: Every row is either parent theorem/adopted limit, exact calibration, formal target, empirical hypothesis, or programme no-go. Parent-owned mathematics receives no novelty credit.

rows.statement: Any frozen finite deterministic network of finite local adaptive units and finite topology/configuration states flattens exactly to one finite-state transducer over the global product state.
rows.consequence: Local adaptive units/topology do not establish a new computational class at finite scope.

rows.statement: A common universal execution basis plus separately hand-authored target-specific compilers is insufficient evidence for a fundamental machine-intelligence substrate because the compiler can encode the architecture-specific prior.
rows.consequence: Charge compiler description/build/search cost; prefer one frozen uniform compiler or developmental acquisition.

rows.statement: For n independent binary state cells with n-bit input and local XOR update, a flat explicit transition table has 4^n state-input entries while factored and ordinary-program execution use O(n) XOR operations.
rows.consequence: Factorization matters; flat-state equivalence does not select a privileged cognitive basis because a general program also preserves compact structure.

rows.statement: At registered model assumptions, a sufficiently expressive typed program/computation-graph representation compactly realizes neural/differentiable, production/symbolic, probabilistic/factorized, and programmatic families; family-specific compilers/algorithms remain prior information.
rows.consequence: Cross-paradigm execution representation is too weak for GMI novelty.

rows.statement: A finite fully specified costed developmental configuration process is a stochastic-shortest-path / metalevel MDP instance under standard assumptions.
rows.consequence: Novelty must come from compact structural prediction/generalization, not merely defining a costed state graph.

rows.statement: For ecology P and morphology proposal prior Q, expected ideal code/search burden is H(P)+D_KL(P||Q). With build cost B and horizon N, expected lifetime burden is B+N[H(P)+D_KL(P||Q)].
rows.consequence: One morphology can dominate because its inductive/proposal bias matches ecology sufficiently well to repay build cost; this is not GMI novelty.

rows.statement: For the registered structured-vs-uniform proposal distributions, the exact ecology/horizon phase boundary is p*(H,B)=[ln(2.5)+B/H]/ln4.
A prefix-tree/code morphology mechanically induces proposal probabilities via Kraft weights; the registered tree structures yield exact expected-burden and horizon-dependent phase boundaries.
rows.consequence: Validates structure->geometry methodology where the mapping is known analytically.

rows.statement: Under a pre-frozen source-coding protocol, label-free exhaustive search over all 13 valid registered code structures recovered all five prospectively predicted morphology regions at p={0.10,0.25,0.50,0.75,0.90}.
rows.consequence: The prediction->neutral search->post-hoc classification pipeline works in a mature parent domain; no GMI credit.

rows.statement: In #323's registered OCM-like morphology, developmental history moved the eventual verified solution earlier in proposal order on 2536/2741 fresh targets (92.5%), median 1.91 bits search saved, while target solutions were absent from history.
rows.claim_boundary: Single registered grammar/morphology family; does not establish cross-paradigm structure->geometry law or K2.

rows.statement: Fixed-portfolio ecology-feature->algorithm choice is classical algorithm selection; experience-conditioned future priors/learning algorithms are meta-learning; cost-aware computation choice is rational metareasoning.
rows.consequence: Track B must generate morphology endogenously and predict geometry from structure, not merely select from a supplied portfolio.

rows.statement: Pre-target compact structural signatures can predict a morphology's proposal/update/resource geometry and first-verified-solution burden on held-out tasks/ecologies better than strongest algorithm-selection/performance-prediction parents.
The same invariant family predicts developmental burden/frontier transitions across materially different morphology paradigms and held-out ecologies.
A theory-predicted phase-diagram hole can be filled by neutral search discovering a morphology not developmentally/resource-equivalent to every applicable registered known parent.

Universal/program representation + domain-specific compilers + AutoML/NAS/program evolution + meta-learning + algorithm selection + rational metareasoning + information theory may fully explain the complete Track-B signature.
